stories.title: Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Silverstein Properties announced that Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP has signed a new lease for 11,167 square feet of office space on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center. The lease establishes a New York office for the firm, an elite litigation boutique.“Dunn Isaacson Rhee represents the caliber of organization that continues to define 7 World Trade Center as one of Downtown Manhattan’s premier office destinations,” said Keith Cody, Head of Commercial Leasing at Silverstein Properties. “Today’s leading firms are seeking workplaces that reflect their brand, support their people, and provide an exceptional experience for their clients. Through thoughtful design, hospitality-driven amenities, and a commitment to excellence, 7 World Trade Center continues to deliver an environment that meets those expectations.”Tenant representation was provided by Lisa Ann Pollakowski, Cory Gahr and Richard Plehn of Lee & Associates. Ownership was represented in-house by Cody, Gordon Hough, and Harlan Strader, with CBRE agency leasing support from MaryAnn Tighe and team. The post Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP leases 11,167 SF at 7 World Trade Center, Manhattan.
Law firm office tenant signals downtown Manhattan office market demand recovery.
No direct multifamily development signal; office-focused asset.
stories.summary: Dunn Isaacson Rhee, an elite litigation boutique, signed a lease for 11,167 square feet on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center in lower Manhattan, establishing its first New York office. Silverstein Properties highlighted the firm as representative of premium tenancy. The lease reflects selective institutional tenant interest in trophy downtown office assets post-pandemic.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing is a distinct capital stack; however, sustained office occupancy in lower Manhattan may support adjacent mixed-use and residential demand if it signals broader neighborhood revitalization and workforce retention in lower Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: Newmark Closes Note Sale on San Pedro Adaptive Reuse
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the sale of a note secured by Topaz Tower, a fully entitled adaptive reuse development project located at 222 W. 6th St. in San Pedro. The 12-story, 309,732-square-foot office tower is entitled for conversion to 246 market-rate multifamily units. Executive Managing Director Ryan Plummer, Co-Head of U.S. Capital Markets Kevin Shannon, Vice Chairman Ken White, Senior Managing Director Chris Benton and Managing Director Anthony Muhlstein represented the lender. The buyer was 222 PV Harbor View, LLC, a private Los Angeles-based residential developer. “Topaz Tower represents an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire a fully entitled coastal high-rise multifamily conversion with scale, ocean views and an immediate execution path in a rapidly evolving submarket,” said Plummer. Topaz Tower Apartments will include a mix of studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences with an average unit size of 835 square feet. Planned amenities include a rooftop deck with a resort-style pool, ocean-view units, balconies and high ceilings. The post Newmark Closes Note Sale on San Pedro Adaptive Reuse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 222 PV Harbor View LLC acquired fully entitled adaptive reuse development in San Pedro, CA.
Topaz Tower: 246 market-rate units, 12-story conversion from office tower, ocean views, immediate execution path.
Note sale signals lender confidence and residential developer capitalization for entitled coastal CA deals.
stories.summary: Newmark closed the sale of a note secured by Topaz Tower, a fully entitled 309,732-square-foot adaptive reuse development at 222 W. 6th St. in San Pedro. The 12-story office tower is permitted for conversion to 246 market-rate multifamily units with an average unit size of 835 square feet, including studio through three-bedroom layouts and resort-style amenities. Buyer 222 PV Harbor View LLC is a Los Angeles-based residential developer acquiring the asset with clear execution path.
stories.impact: Strong signal of adaptive reuse execution momentum and capital availability for coastal Southern California multifamily conversion. San Pedro is rapidly evolving—this entitled high-rise deal with scale and ocean views confirms developer appetite for underutilized office towers in walkable, amenity-rich submarkets. Lender confidence in note sale suggests REITs and debt funds recognize conversion IRRs even in modest LA submarkets; competitive pressure for titled CA deals is rising.

stories.title: Venture X Coworking Location to Open in Pompano Beach
stories.excerpt: Priddy Spaces has signed a 20,000-square-foot lease for a Venture X coworking location in Pompano Beach, Fla. The coworking operator signed a 10-year lease at a 44,102-square-foot office property within Grover Corlew’s Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. Located at 2335 East Atlantic Boulevard, the four-story office building sits two blocks east of Dixie Highway and was constructed in 2020. The coworking outpost — which will span the building’s second, third and fourth floors — will feature 85 private office suites and four meeting rooms. It’s expected to open next year. “Pompano Beach is experiencing one of the most exciting transformations in South Florida,” Kevin Priddy, co-founder and CEO of Priddy Spaces, said in a statement. “The combination of new residential development, improved infrastructure, vibrant dining and retail, and its proximity to the beach has created an environment where businesses and talent want to be.” Pompano Beach, long a working-class town, is seeing a rush of luxury condo development along its coast, from the likes of Miami-based Related Group and other developers. West Palm Beach-based Priddy Spaces is a franchisee of Venture X, operating five locations in South Florida, with Vast Coworking Group serving as the franchisor. Private equity firm New State Capital Partners purchased Vast Coworking Group earlier this year for an undisclosed amount. Priddy Spaces operates a Venture X location in nearby Boca Raton at Grover Corlew’s Palmetto Central office campus. The four-acre Mayla Pompano mixed-use development includes a 355-unit apartment building and two other office properties. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Venture X signs 20,000 SF lease across three floors in Pompano Beach, FL office building.
Coworking at Mayla Pompano mixed-use development; 85 private suites, 10-year lease.
Signals talent and business attraction to Pompano Beach amid residential/retail/infrastructure boom.
stories.summary: Priddy Spaces signed a 10-year, 20,000-square-foot lease for a Venture X coworking location at 2335 East Atlantic Boulevard in Pompano Beach, Florida, spanning the second, third, and fourth floors of a 2020-built, 44,102-square-foot office property within Grover Corlew's Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. The space will feature 85 private office suites and four meeting rooms, opening in 2025. Operator highlighted Pompano's residential expansion, infrastructure improvements, dining, retail, and beach proximity as drivers.
stories.impact: Coworking tenant success in Pompano Beach signals rising white-collar job attraction and employee relocation to South Florida coastal secondary markets. Mixed-use anchoring with office/coworking supports residential lease-up and rent growth in adjacent multifamily phases. Expect Pompano submarket multifamily rents to benefit from talent in-migration and employer decentralization from Miami; timing to acquire or pipeline residential in the area is favorable before broader recognition drives land costs.

stories.title: Domain Lines Up $176M Financing for Mixed-Income Astoria Rentals
stories.excerpt: The Domain Companies has closed on $175.6 million in financing with Wells Fargo for a new mixed-income housing project called Elara, which will deliver 429 new apartments in Astoria, Queens. Domain’s equity partners on the deal are Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. The financing was brokered by Chris Peck and Nicco Lupo of JLL Capital Markets. “Astoria is one of New York’s most vibrant and culturally rich neighborhoods, and it has long held a special place in Domain’s history,” said Matt Schwartz, co-CEO of Domain Companies.“We’re proud to deepen that connection by delivering a thoughtfully designed residential community that reflects the character of the neighborhood while offering one of the highest-quality living experiences in the market.” The project includes an 18-story building with 330 apartments called Elara East, and a 12-story building with 99 apartments named Elara West. The development includes 107 permanently affordable homes. The buildings are located at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st St, with Elara West anticipated to open in February 2028, and Elara East expected in September 2028. The post Domain Lines Up $176M Financing for Mixed-Income Astoria Rentals appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Domain Companies closes $175.6M financing with Wells Fargo for Elara mixed-income project, Astoria, Queens.
429 apartments across two buildings (330 in Elara East, 99 in Elara West); 107 permanently affordable units.
Delivery: Elara West Feb 2028, Elara East Sept 2028; strong capital stack confidence for mixed-income NYC.
stories.summary: The Domain Companies closed $175.6 million in financing from Wells Fargo for Elara, a 429-unit mixed-income multifamily project in Astoria, Queens, with equity partners Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. The development comprises an 18-story, 330-unit Elara East building and a 12-story, 99-unit Elara West, located at 35-45, 35-33, and 35-42 41st Street, with 107 permanently affordable homes. Elara West opens February 2028; Elara East in September 2028.
stories.impact: Demonstrates strong institutional debt appetite for mixed-income multifamily in Queens, a resilient outer-borough market with cultural amenities and transit access. $175.6M on 429 units (~$409K/unit) shows lenders confident in Astoria absorption and permanence of affordability (likely NYCHA partnership or HPD 421-a alternative). Domain's track record in the neighborhood and permanent affordability positioning derisks capital stack; signals outer-borough mixed-income pipeline remains fundable despite rate environment.

stories.title: La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital, a vertically integrated owner and operator of retail and multifamily properties, has secured a lease with La La Land Café to occupy the mezzanine terrace and café space at its upscale Del Mar Plaza retail destination. La La Land will occupy 1,168 square feet of interior space, with additional sitting and queueing space extending onto the terrace deck. The construction start and grand opening dates are not yet determined. The space was formerly occupied by Pacifica Breeze Café. “We’re proud to be first-to-market attracting a dynamic brand that has grown to over 30 locations since its founding in 2019,” said Brixton Capital founder and chairman Marc Brutten. “We expect the grand opening will be very well attended, and that La La Land Café at Del Mar Plaza will remain a very popular social destination.” Victoria Pappas, Brittney Austin and Linda Rubiola of SHOP Companies represented La La Land, while Brixton Capital represented itself, with support from Andrew Shemirani and Ashley Tiefel at Urban Property Group. Lease terms were not disclosed. The post La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: La La Land Café signs first San Diego location at Brixton Capital's Del Mar Plaza, 1,168 SF.
Café brand has grown to 30+ locations since 2019; mezzanine terrace and interior space.
Retail tenant demand signals continued upscale retail appeal in affluent coastal San Diego.
stories.summary: Brixton Capital secured a lease with La La Land Café, a fast-growing café brand with 30+ locations since 2019, for 1,168 square feet of interior space plus terrace at its upscale Del Mar Plaza retail destination in San Diego. The space was formerly occupied by Pacifica Breeze Café. Construction and grand opening dates are not yet determined; lease terms were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, successful upscale café/retail brand expansion into San Pedro/Del Mar coastal submarkets reflects sustained affluent consumer traffic and supports mixed-use residential projects in premium San Diego locations. Brixton Capital's multifamily portfolio benefits from strong retail anchoring; repeat success suggests demand for higher-density, mixed-use development in coastal Southern California.

stories.title: JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged the sale of Boulder Ponds Senior Living and Round Lake Senior Living, a 216-unit portfolio of seniors housing communities located in Lake Elmo and Arden Hills, Minnesota. JLL’s Seniors Housing Capital Markets team represented the seller, Trident Development, in the transaction and secured the buyer, LTC Properties, Inc. Lifespark will remain the operator of both communities. Developed by Trident Development, the portfolio comprises two purpose-built communities strategically located within the Twin Cities submarkets. Both communities offer independent living, assisted living and memory care services. Boulder Ponds Senior Living, completed in 2020, is a 95-unit community in Lake Elmo located at 192 Jade Trail N. The property has demonstrated strong operating performance and stability, maintaining approximately 98% occupancy. Round Lake Senior Living, which opened in 2023, is a 121-unit community in Arden Hills at 1740 Parkshore Dr. The community benefits from convenient access to major employment centers, retail amenities and healthcare services. The post JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LTC Properties acquires 216-unit seniors housing portfolio in Twin Cities (Lake Elmo, Arden Hills, MN).
Boulder Ponds (95 units, 2020) at 98% occupancy; Round Lake (121 units, 2023) opened recent.
Portfolio sale signals active seniors housing capital and operator continuity (Lifespark) in Midwest.
stories.summary: JLL arranged the sale of Boulder Ponds Senior Living and Round Lake Senior Living, a 216-unit seniors housing portfolio in Lake Elmo and Arden Hills, Minnesota. Boulder Ponds (95 units, completed 2020) maintains ~98% occupancy; Round Lake (121 units, opened 2023) benefits from proximity to employment, retail, and healthcare. LTC Properties acquired the portfolio from developer Trident Development; Lifespark remains operator of both communities.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily signal. Seniors housing is a distinct asset class with different capital sources and lease structures; however, strong occupancy and LTC Properties' acquisition confidence indicate healthy Twin Cities demographic tailwinds (aging population, migration to secondary metros). Population aging and operator appetite for newly stabilized communities in secondary markets support broader residential demand. Trident's successful exit after 1–3 years may free capital for conventional multifamily development elsewhere.

stories.title: AI Wealth Management Platform Vise Grabs 12K SF at 50 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is moving from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District, where it will quadruple its office space to 11,949 square feet. The space spans the second floor of several combined historic townhomes along the Ninth Avenue frontage and therefore has dramatic, over 20 foot-high pitched ceilings and an atrium outdoor garden. Rob Kluge and Brandon Charnas of Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant in the 10-year lease. Howard Hersch, Greg Conen, Jennifer Schreiber and Natalie Serio of Newmark represented the building owner, Tavros Capital, which will build out the space. The asking rent was $150 per square foot. Vise is an AI-driven wealth management platform for independent advisors founded by Samir Vasavada and Runik Mehrotra that launched in November 2019. It hosts over $100 billion in assets and the firm is reported to be valued at over $22 billion. It is currently located in 4,000 square feet of office space at 521 Broadway in SoHo. In searching for new digs, Vise was focused on upgrading both its office and culture. “We worked with ownership on a creative solution whereby the ground-floor retailer, Jen Rubio’s fashion company — now known as Elsa, which was then negotiating their deal — would expand upstairs and take roughly another 4,000 to 5,000 square feet on the West 14th Street side of the floor,” Charnas said. “That allowed us to create a space for Vise that fit both their program and their budget.” “We worked through multiple iterations with ownership and the architect to take what had been one larger floor and create the right long-term home for Vise,” added Kluge. The resulting space primarily overlooks Ninth Avenue and sits directly across from the Apple store, with dramatic vaulted ceilings, tons of light and a build-out being designed specifically around Vise’s needs and specifications. bullets: Vise AI wealth platform leases 11,949 SF at 50 Ninth Avenue, Meatpacking District, Manhattan.
Expanding from 4,000 SF (SoHo) to quad size; 10-year lease at $150/SF; $22B firm valuation.
High-growth fintech tenant signals demand for premium, architect office in central Manhattan.
stories.summary: Vise, an AI-powered wealth management platform valued at $22 billion with $100+ billion in assets under platform, leased 11,949 square feet across the second floor of combined historic townhomes at 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District. The space features over 20-foot-high pitched ceilings, atrium garden, and 10-year lease at $150/SF asking rent. Vise is quadrupling from its prior 4,000-SF SoHo office. Founded November 2019, the firm has scaled rapidly.
stories.impact: Signals sustained high-growth fintech and AI firm office demand in Manhattan, supporting residential market for young professionals and mid-to-senior talent seeking walkable, transit-rich neighborhoods near Meatpacking/Chelsea employment centers. Growth-stage tech firm expansion correlates with strong rent growth and absorption in adjacent residential submarkets; confirms Manhattan's continued appeal for high-margin service firms despite remote-work adoption.

stories.title: SME Capital Forced to Hand Over Hudson Yards Condo Building to Residents
stories.excerpt: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is handing ownership of 441 West 37th Street to the condominium board after an investigation by the New York Attorney General’s office. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023. It then failed to pay bills related to the Hudson Yards property and neglected safety violations, leading to a settlement to pay $700,000, according to Attorney General Letitia James. Built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, the nine-unit building went into foreclosure in 2023. SME never reported to the state that it was the winning bidder in the auction and never acknowledged that it owned the building, leaving residents to pick up the tab for things like a new $15,824 certificate of occupancy, according to the AG. Some of the units were rented out while awaiting buyers, including 35 formerly homeless people who were ousted around the time SME took control of the building, according to The Real Deal. “Private equity firms do not get to pick and choose which laws apply to them,” James said in a statement. “When this company took control of a Manhattan condo building, it took on real legal responsibilities to the homeowners who lived there. For two years, SME Capital dodged those duties while still collecting rent checks. My office will keep holding these firms accountable when they put profits over New Yorkers’ safety.” Balkany could not be reached for comment. bullets: SME Capital Ventures relinquishes ownership of 441 W. 37th St. Hudson Yards condo to board.
Nine-unit 2020-built condo; SME acquired in 2023 foreclosure, failed to pay bills, safety violations.
Settlement: $700K; NY AG enforcement on private equity neglect and resident harm.
stories.summary: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures handed ownership of 441 West 37th Street, a nine-unit Hudson Yards condo built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, to the condominium board after investigation by the New York Attorney General. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023 but failed to pay bills and address safety violations. Settlement required $700,000 payment; residents, including 35 formerly homeless people, were displaced or left unpaid for building operations and compliance costs.
stories.impact: Negative signal for opportunistic foreclosure acquisition strategies and private equity real estate operations in NYC. Regulatory enforcement and resident-protective legal action raise reputational and execution risk for out-of-market or passive capital attempting distressed multifamily/condo acquisitions in New York. Lender and agency scrutiny of foreclosure buyer intent and performance will tighten future underwriting and title requirements, increasing transaction friction and reducing distressed multifamily deal flow in NYC.

stories.title: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery Sells to Integritas Capital for $42M
stories.excerpt: A 170-year-old monastery in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, has sold for $42.25 million. The Sisters of the Visitation’s 7.5-acre campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard — a campus behind 30-foot stone walls, with a monastery, chapel and school — was bought by a group of Brooklyn-based developers and investors with a history of large residential projects, including leaders of Integritas Capital and Heights Advisors. A petition by the Catholic religious order to sell its real estate was approved by the office of the New York State Attorney General on Monday. Nonprofits are required by New York law to obtain approval when it sells all or most of its assets. The buyer entity, 1137 91 LLC, is led by Brooklyn real estate investor Stephen Palmese, founder of private equity platform Integritas Capital (and a former vice chair at JLL). Passive investors included Rachel Foster, founder and president of Brooklyn housing developer Heights Advisors, alongside the developer’s director, Scott Geddes, as well as Daniel Kodsi and Matthew Kodsi . The longtime professional partners are planning a resort-residential tower in Fort Lauderdale, according to The Real Deal. Palmese’s Integritas is also the lender behind a forthcoming 27-story church-to-residential conversion in Brooklyn’s Fort Greene. The cohort of buyers suggests the historic property’s likely fate as a major mixed-used or residential development. The Visitation Sisters entered into an initial contract in late April, according to the filing, but the school and monastery have been shuttered since 2024, after their numbers dropped too low to sustain full ministry. The Visitation Sisters, formally the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary, were a French order founded in 1610. Their presence in Brooklyn dates back to 1855. The sellers expect net proceeds of $40.9 million, according to the filing, which will be held in escrow under an approved dissolution and distribution of assets plan. bullets: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery sells 7.5-acre Bay Ridge, Brooklyn campus for $42.25M to Integritas Capital-led group.
170-year-old property includes monastery, chapel, school behind 30-foot stone walls.

stories.summary: The Sisters of the Visitation Monastery sold its 7.5-acre Bay Ridge, Brooklyn campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard for $42.25 million to a buyer group led by Stephen Palmese (founder of Integritas Capital and former JLL vice chair), Heights Advisors founder Rachel Foster, and passive investors. The 170-year-old property includes a monastery, chapel, and school within 30-foot stone walls. Buyer entity 1137 91 LLC has a track record in large residential development projects.
stories.impact: Significant Brooklyn land opportunity for large-scale residential redevelopment in Bay Ridge, a gentrifying outer-borough market with strong transit and neighborhood upside. The 7.5-acre footprint—rare for Brooklyn—enables mid-to-large multifamily pipeline or mixed-use repositioning. Experienced residential developer buyer group indicates high-density multifamily intent. Expect rezoning pursuit, CEQR process, and 24–36 month entitlement timeline; early acquisition positions the group ahead of market recognition of Bay Ridge supply/demand tailwinds.

stories.title: Benefit Street Partners Provides $103M Bridge Debt for Texas Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Vantage Communities has secured $103 million in bridge debt to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio in three cities in Texas, Commercial Observer can first report. Benefit Street Partners provided the debt, which will finance the property toward full stabilization and is structured as a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan with a three-year term. Greystone Capital Advisors‘ Drew Fletcher, Bryan Grover, Jesse Kopecky and Cameron Behr arranged the transaction. “Benefit Street Partners recognized the quality of the sponsorship, the assets, and the long-term fundamentals supporting these dynamic Central Texas markets,” said Fletcher. The three assets are split among Vantage at Hutto — a 288-unit complex located at 1051 North Farm to Market 1660 in Hutto, Tex., just outside of Austin; Vantage at McKinney Falls — a 288-unit complex located at 7900 McKinney Falls Parkway in suburban Austin, Tex.; and Vantage at Fair Oaks — a 288-unit complex located at 9135 Dietz Elkhorn Road in Boerne, Tex. outside of San Antonio. All three assets opened in either 2023 or 2024 and feature amenities such as resident clubhouses, fitness centers and resort-style swimming pools. “We were pleased to structure a financing solution that met our clients’ objectives while leveraging the strength of this high-quality, recently delivered portfolio,” added Fletcher in a statement. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Benefit Street Partners provides $103M bridge debt for Vantage Communities' three-property, 864-unit Texas portfolio.
Properties: Hutto (288 units), McKinney Falls, Austin (288 units), Fair Oaks, Boerne (288 units).
Floating-rate interest-only 3-year bridge; Greystone Capital arranged; supports stabilization and refinance.
stories.summary: Vantage Communities secured $103 million in bridge debt from Benefit Street Partners to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio across three Texas markets: Vantage at Hutto (288 units), Vantage at McKinney Falls in suburban Austin (288 units), and Vantage at Fair Oaks in Boerne (288 units). The floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan has a three-year term and finances the properties toward stabilization. Greystone Capital Advisors arranged the transaction.
stories.impact: Strong signal of debt capital confidence in Texas multifamily fundamentals and Vantage's sponsorship quality. Central Texas markets (Austin suburbs, Hill Country) are absorbing growth from tech migration and population in-migration; three-year bridge structure suggests lender confidence in stabilization and exit within cycle. Vantage's ability to secure $103M on recent/stabilizing assets at floating rates indicates cap rates remain compressed and institutional debt appetite for quality multifamily in secondary Texas metros is robust. Competitive positioning for new development in Hutto, Austin suburbs, and Hill Country is favorable.
